## Wave 3 Summary

This wave adjudicates and operationalizes the **structural status** of the disorder→Goldstone-mass route to the 170× dark-matter mass shortfall, building DIRECTLY on the inv5 Imry-Ma FAIL (NOT a fresh first compute). The prior state is unambiguous (grounding catch #1):

- `INV5-W2-4-GOLDSTONE-MASS-FROM-DISORDER` (FAIL): the Imry-Ma random-field route — random field = the substrate's own non-C² Josephson couplings (su(2) J_su2=0.059, u(1) J_u1=0.038); ordered backbone = C² coset (J_C2=0.933) — gave `m_G = h_rf/ξ_Larkin = 0.003185 M_KK` (construction A, Larkin length ξ_Larkin = J_C2/h_rf = 17.115 bonds), failing LEG1 (no enhancement: enh = m_G/ω_L1 = 0.0231 < 1) while staying below the pair-breaking edge (LEG2: x_G < 1). `frac170 = m_G/(170·Δ_BCS) = 4.036e-05` — the route reached **4×10⁻⁵ of the 170× target**.
- The inv5 bracket's most aggressive reading (construction E: whole C²-backbone as random field, ξ=1 bond) reached only `frac170 = J_C2/(170·Δ_BCS) ≈ 0.0118` — the disorder-family ceiling.

The genuinely-open question is therefore NOT "does Imry-Ma close the 170×" (it does not — settled FAIL) but **"is the disorder→Goldstone-mass route STRUCTURALLY CLOSED by the Josephson-graph coupling-scale ceiling, or does a non-Imry-Ma mechanism (a different ξ_disorder scaling from the full coupling distribution — e.g. the Cheeger lattice-Laplacian connectivity gap, a rare-region/heavy-tail of the distribution) survive?"** The structural anchor is `atlas-spectral-geometer-collab §5` (the Cheeger inequality on the SU(3) Josephson tessellation: the Goldstone mass IS the lattice-Laplacian spectral gap, `m_G ≥ h(L)/2` with `h(L) ~ 2J_C2/Vol(cell)`), which unifies the disorder route and the connectivity route under one ceiling.

- **WORKSHOP** (`S116-W3-DISORDER-CLOSURE`, 2 agents): structural-closure adjudication — `landau-condensed-matter-theorist` (structural-closure pole) × `phonon-first-cosmologist` (surviving-channel pole). R1/R2/R3 → STRUCTURAL VERDICT (closed-by-graph-scale-wall vs open-via-surviving-channel).
- **COMPUTE** (`S116-W3-GOLDSTONE-M2`, landau): computes the concrete non-Imry-Ma candidate (the Cheeger / lattice-Laplacian connectivity gap from the Josephson J-matrix) AND pins the Josephson-graph ceiling, reloading the inv5 disorder bracket. Verdict rubric pre-registers BOTH branches: surviving mechanism (PASS/INFO) vs structural-closure ceiling (FAIL). `m²~1/ξ_disorder²` with the connectivity ξ_eff; pre-registers `frac170` PASS band vs the 170× target.

**Gate-type mix**: workshop × 1 + compute × 1 (MIXED wave).

## Wave 3 Decision Point Prerequisites

- **S116-W3-GOLDSTONE-M2 is CONDITIONAL on the workshop verdict in its READING, not in its execution.** The compute is fully runnable in parallel with (or after) the workshop: its numerical content (the Cheeger/lattice-Laplacian connectivity mass, the disorder-family ceiling reload, frac170) is the same regardless of the workshop outcome. The workshop SELECTS which branch is the headline reading; the compute's `machinery_pin_map.surviving_mechanism` defaults to `cheeger_connectivity` (the collab-§5-grounded concrete candidate) and consumes a workshop-named mechanism ONLY if the workshop identifies a concrete one beyond Cheeger/connectivity. There is therefore **no mechanical-closure / upstream-block risk** — the compute does not hard-gate on a workshop verdict line (workshops emit none).
- **Recommended dispatch order**: run the workshop first (or concurrently); if the workshop names a concrete surviving mechanism distinct from the Cheeger/connectivity candidate, pass its identifier into the compute's `surviving_mechanism` pin before the compute fires. If the workshop converges on structural closure (the Landau-pole reading), the compute runs as the ceiling pin with the Cheeger/connectivity candidate as the most-optimistic in-family mechanism.
- **Input prerequisites (both gates)**: all consume already-landed substrate data — `INV5-W2-4-GOLDSTONE-MASS-FROM-DISORDER` verdict + `inv5_w2_4_goldstone_mass_disorder.npz`, `s48_goldstone_mass.npz` (rho_s, BCS-floor, SA-mass=0 wall), `s29b_josephson_coupling.npz` (the J-matrix for the graph Laplacian), `canonical_constants.py` (J_C2, J_su2, J_u1, ω_L1, Δ_BCS). No unmet prereq; no investigation-track dependency.

       the long Larkin length — the substrate's stiffest bond sets the gap]

    Step 4 (Ratio — surviving mechanism vs Imry-Ma baseline):
      m_G^Ch / m_G^IM = (J_C2 / 1) / (h_rf / ξ_Larkin) = J_C2 · ξ_Larkin / h_rf
                      = 0.933 · 17.115 / 0.054514 = 293        [the connectivity mass is ~293× larger]

    Step 5 (Direction from canonical form — the SIGN read-off):
      ξ_eff = 1 bond  <  ξ_Larkin = 17.115 bonds  (SMALLER)  AND  E_eff = J_C2 > h_rf  (LARGER).
      ∂m_G/∂ξ_disorder = −E_disorder / ξ_disorder² < 0  ⇒ m_G strictly DECREASES in ξ_disorder
      ⇒ SHORTER ξ_eff ⇒ LARGER m_G. Therefore m_G^Ch > m_G^IM:  SIGN of (m_G^Ch − m_G^IM) is POSITIVE.
      [the surviving mechanism's only lever is a SHORTER disorder length; the inv5 gate used the LONG
       Larkin length, which is why Imry-Ma under-shot — the connectivity gap is the short-ξ reading.]

    Step 6 (Ceiling — the binding wall):
      E_disorder ≤ max Josephson coupling = J_C2  (disorder energy is the coupling SPREAD; it cannot
        exceed the largest coupling on the graph)  AND  ξ_disorder ≥ 1 bond  (sub-lattice domains
        forbidden)  ⇒  m_G = E/ξ ≤ J_C2 / 1 = J_C2 = 0.933 M_KK.
      ⇒ frac170 = m_G/(170·Δ_BCS) ≤ J_C2/(170·Δ_BCS) = 0.933/78.9233 = 0.011822.
      Pair-breaking-edge cross-check at the ceiling: ω_G^ceiling = m_G^ceiling/sqrt(rho_s)
        = 0.933/sqrt(7.962) = 0.933/2.822 = 0.3306;  x_G^ceiling = 0.3306/(2·0.4642547) = 0.356 < 1
        ⇒ the ceiling mode IS below the pair-breaking edge (a VALID DM candidate) — the binding wall is
        the COUPLING-SCALE ceiling (frac170 ≤ 0.0118), NOT the pair-breaking edge (which is not even
        reached at the ceiling). To reach the 170× target (x_G ≈ 30) one would need BOTH to exceed the
        graph coupling scale (impossible for graph-derived disorder) AND to push ~30× above the edge
        (destroying the quasiparticle) — the coupling-scale wall is hit first.

    Conclusion: the surviving (connectivity) mechanism gives a LARGER mass than Imry-Ma (SIGN = POSITIVE,
      ξ_eff smaller) — so SIGN=PASS — but frac170 ≤ 0.0118 ≪ 1 (MAGNITUDE = FAIL): the disorder/
      connectivity route is structurally closed ~85× short of the 170× target. Composite (collapse rule,
      gate-verdicts.md): sign=PASS ∧ magnitude=FAIL ∧ regime=VALID ⇒ FAIL. The FAIL maps the structural-
      closure corridor: the Josephson-graph cannot anchor the 170× DM mass; it must come from a scale
      OUTSIDE the graph (Reading B — graph-unanchored, abundance-fixed but magnitude-free, like M_KK).

# ---- Verdict rubric (BOTH branches pre-registered) ----
PASS_meaning: >
  BRANCH A (surviving mechanism). frac170 ≥ 0.5 with SIGN=PASS (m_G^mechanism > the inv5 Imry-Ma
  baseline) and REGIME=VALID (the mode stays below the pair-breaking edge): a non-Imry-Ma disorder/
  connectivity mechanism reaches ≥ 50% of the 170× target. Solution-space: the disorder→Goldstone-mass
  route SURVIVES the closed corridors — the Josephson-graph CAN anchor (most of) the DM structure-
  formation mass; the HK-170X-DM gap is (substantially) closed by the graph spectral gap, and the
  Reading-A pole of S116-W3-DISORDER-CLOSURE is confirmed.
FAIL_meaning: >
  BRANCH B (structural closure — the physically-expected outcome). frac170 ≤ frac170_ceiling_family ≈
  0.0118 = J_C2/(170·Δ_BCS): the surviving mechanism is bounded by the Josephson-graph coupling scale
  (m_G ≤ J_C2 ≈ 2Δ_BCS), ~85× short of the 170× target — even though SIGN=PASS (the connectivity gap is
  ~293× the Imry-Ma baseline, the correct direction). Solution-space: the disorder/connectivity route is
  STRUCTURALLY CLOSED — every graph-derived mechanism caps at the coupling scale; the 170× DM mass cannot
  be anchored to the Josephson graph and must come from a scale OUTSIDE it (Reading B of WS-S112-4: the
  Leggett-DM mass is graph-unanchored, abundance-fixed but magnitude-free, structurally like M_KK). This
  FAIL closes the disorder corridor and pins the ceiling formula frac170 ≤ J_C2/(170·Δ_BCS) — an
  informative wall, per "All Results Are Good Results."
INFO_meaning: >
  PARTIAL survival. frac170_ceiling_family < frac170 < 0.5 with SIGN=PASS: a mechanism that BEATS the
  disorder-family construction-E ceiling but does not close the 170× target — the route is OPEN at a
  reduced shortfall (the new factor is reported). Also the INFO landing if REGIME=MARGINAL/BREAKDOWN
  (the mechanism's mass pushes toward/above the pair-breaking edge, jeopardizing the DM-survival
  argument): the mass enhancement exists but at the cost of the below-edge protection — a tension the
  next session's DM-mass-anchor gate inherits. This is the registry state named in INFO.

  PHONONIC. The U(1)₇ phase Goldstone IS the substrate's broken-phase boson (PROVED ungaugeable
  [iK_7,D_K]=0, N4 BROKEN; SA-mass=0 EXACT S48 wall #7 — the spectral action cannot mass it, so any
  mass is a graph spectral moment, NOT a spectral-action term). Its mass is the lattice-Laplacian
  spectral gap (Cheeger isoperimetric constant) of the SU(3) Josephson tessellation — the lowest
  nonzero eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian on phase fluctuations — OR the random-field pinning gap
  (Imry-Ma), both built from the SAME couplings {J_C2, J_su2, J_u1}. The flow is D_K (0,0)-sector
  eigenvalues → Josephson couplings → graph Laplacian λ_1 / Imry-Ma pinning → m_G → DM structure-
  formation mass → halo/LSS phenomenology (measured). The 170× "problem" is the container-thinking

  a mass ~85× above itself: the substrate IS the Josephson graph, and a graph cannot pin its own phase

  is anchored OUTSIDE the graph scale (not a correction IN a container); the substrate predicts the
  DM abundance (Leggett 0.6%-Planck, below-edge protected) but not, on this route, its magnitude.

## Wave 3 → Next-Session Decision Point

The compute's verdict selects the forward routing (consumed by `/rclab-plan` at S117 plan-freeze):

- **FAIL (Branch B, structural closure — expected)**: the disorder/connectivity corridor is closed; pin the ceiling formula `frac170 ≤ J_C2/(170·Δ_BCS) ≈ 0.012` and route the DM-mass-anchor question to the Reading-B "Josephson-graph-unanchored" conclusion. Carry-forward: a session-promotion gate (mack/little sole-writer) recording the HK-170X-DM gap as CLOSED-ON-DISORDER-ROUTE / OPEN-ONLY-VIA-OUT-OF-GRAPH-SCALE in atlas-04 DM-properties + open-channel-ledger §DMMASS. This is NOT a re-compute — it is a registry-state update consuming this gate's verdict.
- **INFO (partial survival)**: a mechanism beats the in-family ceiling but does not close the target; carry-forward a 4-field spec for the next-session gate testing the named mechanism at the reduced shortfall (what: the partial-survival mechanism's m_G at full L_max / fold-epoch resolution; inputs: this gate's npz + the workshop-named construction; gate: frac170 vs the new reduced factor; effort: medium).
- **PASS (Branch A, surviving mechanism)**: the route survives; carry-forward the surviving mechanism as a new DM-mass-anchor candidate — a Stage-1 registry candidate + a follow-up gate cross-checking the abundance (Leggett 0.6%-Planck) is NOT degraded by the heavier mass (the W2-2 two-scale concern).

The workshop's STRUCTURAL VERDICT (CLOSED-BY-GRAPH-SCALE-WALL vs OPEN-VIA-<named-mechanism>) is the qualitative companion to the compute's quantitative frac170 verdict; both land this session.

## Wave 3 Machinery-Enumeration Pin (COMPUTE gate only)

Aggregate of `S116-W3-GOLDSTONE-M2.machinery_pin_map` (the only compute gate; the workshop contributes no producing script). For `_yaml_gate_validator.py` / `_pru_cardinality_audit.py`:

|:----|:------|
| N_eval | SU(3) Josephson unit-cell graph (8 bonds: 4 C² + 3 su(2) + 1 u(1)); Fiedler λ_1 of the s29b-J-matrix-weighted Laplacian; + inv5 5-construction disorder bracket reload |
| L_max | 10 |
| scan_range | N/A — single-point at tau_fold=0.190 |
| step_size | N/A — deterministic single-point |
| tolerance | 1e-9 (float64; outputs to 4 sig figs) |
| scheme | JOSEPHSON-GRAPH-CHEEGER-CONNECTIVITY-CEILING |
| convention | GOLDSTONE-MASS-FROM-LATTICE-LAPLACIAN-FIEDLER-GAP-VS-DISORDER-FAMILY-CEILING |
| random_seed | N/A — deterministic |

PRU note: the `surviving_mechanism` conditional pin is the ONLY workshop-coupled free parameter; it is pinned to a default (`cheeger_connectivity`) so the gate is PRU-complete (D_PRU_raw = 0) and runnable WITHOUT the workshop verdict — the workshop only swaps the default for a named mechanism if one is identified. No other parameter is workshop-dependent.
